nodes.text: Ha! A visitor! Grab a stave or stand clear. Either way, talk loud, I'm working.
Talk while I work. The hoops don't ring themselves.

choices.text: How does a barrel even work?

nodes.text: Count with me: the Flagon's cellar, Signy's stores, Koll's quench water, Wyn's steeping casks, every wagon on the High Road, and the ferry down at the ford ships its catch in *my* wet-casks. Half this city is things that need holding. Ask Stig who the Timberway actually runs on. Go on. Ask him with me watching.

Thirty staves, every one bent against its will, and an iron hoop driven on until the whole thing sits round and tight. No glue, no nails. Fire, water, and a mallet. Balla forges my hoops and swears coopering is smithing for people afraid of fire. I let her have that one. My barrels float. Her anvils don't.

My mother, on a coast you've never heard of, where a leaky cask meant a hungry winter. She'd have called this mountain work soft. Nobody drowns if I'm sloppy. Then she'd have inspected every hoop in this shop anyway. I still build like she's coming by later.
Ring true! And if you ever buy a barrel that leaks, it isn't mine. Bring it anyway, I'll fix it.
